**Proposed mechanism:** FGFR3 (HGNC:3613) —LEADS_TO→ Achondroplasia (HP:0000274); FGF23 (HGNC:3613) —DECREASES→ Phosphate (CHEBI:17753); Phosphate (CHEBI:17753) —INCREASES→ Hyperphosphatemia (HP:0003085); Hyperphosphatemia (HP:0003085) —LEADS_TO→ Tumoral calcinosis (HP:0030075); FGF23 (HGNC:3613) —DISRUPTS→ Phosphate Homeostasis (GO:0006773); Phosphate Homeostasis (GO:0006773) —DECREASES→ Phosphate (CHEBI:17753). Gain-of-function mutations in FGFR3 lead to achondroplasia. Loss-of-function mutations in FGF23 disrupt phosphate homeostasis, leading to hyperphosphatemia and tumoral calcinosis. Both genes are critical regulators of bone development and mineral metabolism, thus representing a shared module despite different functional consequences.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for achondroplasia and tumoral calcinosis, or if mutations in FGF23 are found to cause achondroplasia, or mutations in FGFR3 are found to cause tumoral calcinosis. _(variant: Common variants in FGFR3 or FGF23 (AF > 0.01) that are not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of FGF23 and FGFR3 in bone and mineral metabolism could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting phosphate regulation or bone growth for both achondroplasia and tumoral calcinosis.
